title: Athletics
status: draft: written 18 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 4 Creative Arts; not yet checked by a CBC Creative Arts teacher; not loaded by the live tutor
notes: Sprint starts are practised on the field with commands; questions ask only for order and form.

skills.key_step: The child orders the commands "On your marks, set, go", and describes the medium and elongated starts.

floor.prerequisite: Moves in a chosen direction with control.
floor.question: What do you do when told to stop in a game?

steps: On your marks: hands behind the line, knee down.
Go: push hard and drive forward.

board.do: At set, where are the hips?
Up, a little higher than the shoulders.

misconceptions.ask: What is the first command at the start?
misconceptions.repair: Practise the three commands in a line.

misconceptions.ask: What happens to the hips at Set?
misconceptions.repair: Show the position at Set and ask where the weight is.

misconceptions.ask: In which start are the feet furthest apart?
misconceptions.repair: Mark the foot places in the sand for each start.

misconceptions.ask: Where do the eyes look at the start?
misconceptions.repair: Say: you race your own lane.

checks.question: Put in order: set, go, on your marks.
At "set", where do the hips go?

skills.key_step: The child describes good sprinting: on the balls of the feet, arms swinging forward and back, eyes ahead, running through the line.
steps: Run on the balls of the feet.
contexts: chasing a ball in a game

misconceptions.ask: How do the arms swing in sprinting?
misconceptions.repair: Run slowly with arms across and with arms forward and back.

misconceptions.ask: Which part of the foot does a sprinter use?
misconceptions.repair: Run on the heels for a few steps and feel the slowing.

listen_for: Slows down and stops before it
misconceptions.ask: What does a sprinter do at the finish line?
misconceptions.repair: Run to a line and run through it.

misconceptions.ask: Where does a sprinter look when running?
misconceptions.repair: Run looking ahead and notice the body stay straight.

checks.question: Do sprinters run on their heels or the balls of their feet?

skills.key_step: The child names the flag colours in order (black, white, red, white, green) and what each means.

floor.prerequisite: Knows occasions when the flag is raised (Grade 3).
floor.question: Name one day the flag is raised.
floor.answer: any national day or a school assembly

steps: Name the colours top to bottom.
Black: the people; red: the struggle; green: the land; white: peace.
Shield and spears: defence of freedom.
contexts: painting a flag for an athletics event

board.do: Wait for the struggle for freedom.

misconceptions.ask: Which colour is at the top of the Kenyan flag?
misconceptions.repair: Colour the stripes in order and check with a real flag.

misconceptions.ask: What does the red in the Kenyan flag stand for?
misconceptions.repair: Match each colour to its meaning on a card.

misconceptions.ask: Why is the Kenyan flag flown at an event?
misconceptions.repair: Ask where the flag flies and what it stands for.

misconceptions.ask: What does the shield and spears on the Kenyan flag stand for?
misconceptions.repair: Read the meaning together: they defend freedom.

checks.question: What does green stand for on the flag?
Why is the flag flown at an athletics event?
checks.answer: to show national pride and unity
